journal: Journal of Chemical and Engineering Data 26, 388-391
title: Solubility of carbon dioxide in liquid water and of water in gaseous carbon dioxide in the range 0.2-5 MPa and at temperatures up to 473 K
experimental_method: Static method in a thermostatted measuring tube with cathetometer volume readings and dead-weight manometer pressure: dew-point pressures and p-V isotherms down to 0.2 MPa for water + CO2 mixtures of fixed composition, and boiling-point pressures near pure water.
uncertainties_stated: temperature controlled within +-5 mK (Tinsley Pt thermometer, IPTS-68); pressure overall accuracy 0.03 %; tube volume calibration 0.09 %; cathetometer +-0.006 mm; correction for 1e-9 mol air in the tube; difference between dew and boiling points of pure water 0.002-0.003 MPa
quality_remarks: Table I contains p-V isotherm points beyond the dew points (single-phase gas, with water mole fraction x_1 = overall composition). Only the dew-point rows (flag d) are mapped as water content of the gas phase. The PDF starts with the end of another article (page 388, glossary and references of a chromatography paper) and the figures on page 390 are not data. Water was twice distilled; CO2 from Na2CO3 + H2SO4, dried and liquefied; purity not stated numerically.
not_extracted_tables: Table III (second cross virial coefficient B12: not in scope)
Table IV (Henry constants H_p calculated by the authors by extrapolation from the data and literature comparison columns: derived)

row_counts.Table 1: printed 142 (p,V) pairs in 14 blocks (14 dew points); written 142 data rows plus 14 label rows
row_counts.Table 2: printed 42 cells (7 T x 6 x_1), 33 values and 9 printed blanks; written 42 data rows (9 with empty p) plus 6 label rows

extraction_notes: Text layer matched the image in every cell (checked blocks at 250 dpi crops). Sanity: within each Table I block p decreases monotonically while V increases; dew pressure rises with T at fixed x_1; Table II p increases with T and with decreasing x_1 in each row. Block x_1=0.9347 has only the dew-point pair. Several printed (p,V) lines have fewer than four pairs; blocks end with shorter lines; stacking order is pair-column wise.
